headline: National Housing Bank appoints forensic auditor for SRG Housing Finance
hook: Forensic audit ordered into lender accounts
summary: The National Housing Bank has appointed ASA & Associates LLP to conduct a forensic audit of SRG Housing Finance following allegations of fictitious loan accounts valued at ₹300–400 crore. The investigation will also examine repayment record manipulation and possible fund diversion, scrutinising loan disbursements and asset classifications. The findings from this probe could trigger regulatory actions and impact the housing finance company's financial outlook. Retail investors holding shares in the company face heightened governance and asset quality risks.
whats_next: Submission of the forensic audit findings to National Housing Bank
why_it_matters: Governance risks cloud the lender's asset quality and valuation.
winners_losers: Short-sellers gain / SRG Housing shareholders hurt

headline: SRG Housing Finance initiates a forensic audit
hook: Governance red flag at SRG Housing
summary: SRG Housing Finance Limited has officially informed the stock exchanges that a forensic audit has been initiated. Forensic audits are typically undertaken by companies to investigate financial discrepancies, irregularities, or specific concerns raised by regulators or auditors. For Indian retail investors holding shares in the company, this disclosure introduces significant corporate governance uncertainty until the audit findings are made public.
whats_next: Exchange disclosures regarding audit findings and completion
why_it_matters: Higher governance risk clouds the near-term outlook for your holding

headline: SRG Housing Finance clarifies on false news article in Economic Times
summary: SRG Housing Finance Limited has officially clarified to the stock exchanges regarding a false news article published in The Economic Times. The clarification was issued under Regulation 30(11) of SEBI listing regulations to address market rumours. Retail investors should note official clarifications when assessing the veracity of media reports concerning listed companies.
why_it_matters: Clears up unverified media reports affecting the stock.

headline: National Housing Bank orders forensic audit of SRG Housing Finance over dubious lending
hook: Forensic audit targets alleged loan discrepancies
summary: The National Housing Bank has initiated a forensic audit of SRG Housing Finance following growing concerns over dubious lending practices. The investigation will examine allegations of fictitious loans, unsupported accounts, and repayment discrepancies ranging from ₹300 to ₹400 crore. Auditors will review consumer data and loan origination processes to uncover potential fraud. Retail investors holding stock in the company face heightened regulatory and governance risks.
whats_next: Forensic audit findings submission to National Housing Bank
why_it_matters: Governance concerns trigger sharp risks for SRG Housing shareholders.

headline: SRG Housing Finance reports zero overdues and considers capital infusion
hook: Clean loan book at SRG Housing
summary: SRG Housing Finance has reported zero overdues in its loan portfolio and is evaluating options for a capital infusion. This financial health indicator reflects strong asset quality for the housing finance company. Retail investors tracking smaller housing financiers should note the pristine asset quality metrics. Capital raising could dilute existing equity while supporting loan book expansion.
why_it_matters: Zero overdues signal strong asset quality for the lender.
winners_losers: SRG Housing gains / no clear losers
